small_guidance:
- The conv3d kernel is the dominant cost; sweep larger BLOCK_SP variants and add configs with smaller BLOCK_SP (64, 128) paired with num_warps=2 to reduce register pressure from the fully-unrolled (IC=3, KD=KH=KW=4 = 192 iters) inner loop. Also try num_stages=4 for the wider tiles.
- Each program reloads the same (IC, KD, KH, KW) slab for one (B, OC) pair; tile OC inside a single program (e.g. BLOCK_OC=4 or 8) so the input loads are amortized across multiple output channels — change grid to (B * ceil(OC/BLOCK_OC), sp_tiles) and accumulate `BLOCK_OC × BLOCK_SP` outputs per program, then apply hardswish before storing.
- Keys for autotune should include B (currently fine) but consider hoisting `id_*HW + ih_*W + iw_` index math out of the innermost kw loop to reduce integer ops; precompute `oh*W+ow` once per tile.
large_guidance:
- Restructure conv3d as an im2col-style GEMM: one program per (B, OC tile, output-spatial tile) doing a tiled matmul with K = IC*KD*KH*KW = 192. Use `tl.dot` with BLOCK_M (OC tile, e.g. 16) × BLOCK_N (spatial tile, e.g. 64–128) × BLOCK_K (32 or 64), computing input gather offsets implicitly inside the K loop. This will be vastly faster than the current scalar FMA accumulation pattern.
- Fuse hardswish into the GEMM epilogue (already partially done) and additionally compute per-channel partial sums for the mean within the same kernel by reducing across the spatial tile and atomic-adding into a `[B, OC]` sum buffer plus a `[B, OC]` sumsq buffer — then GroupNorm + mean becomes a tiny `(B, num_groups)` kernel that only reads B*OC scalars (no need to materialize/reread the full `[B, OC, S]` activation).
- Alternatively, since post-mean we only need per-channel scalar sum and sumsq for GroupNorm-then-mean (because mean of (γ·(x-μ)/σ + β) over spatial = γ·(mean(x)-μ)/σ + β), avoid writing conv_out at all: have the conv kernel accumulate sum(hardswish(conv)) and sum(hardswish(conv)^2) per (B, OC) directly via atomics or via a second reduction-only pass over a persistent tile. This eliminates the 1024·16·13·29·29 ≈ 180M-element intermediate write/read.
